title: Fading Colors Question Pool
instructions: Do not let the rooms lose their color.
Read the clues around the map. Clues teach you what you need for that same quest.
Complete the main quest in each room.
A wrong main-quest answer loses that room and makes the other active rooms fade faster.
Side quests are optional. Complete them before the final main quest to earn a time-pause reward.

clues.title: Three paint colors
clues.text: In a simple artist's color wheel, red, yellow, and blue are the main paint colors. They are called primary colors.

clues.title: Mixing paint
clues.text: Red + yellow makes orange. Yellow + blue makes green. Blue + red makes purple. These are simple rules for paint; screen light works differently.

stages.question: Which three colors are the traditional paint primaries?
stages.feedback: Red, yellow, and blue are the traditional primary colors for paint.

stages.question: What color do red and yellow paint make?
stages.feedback: Red mixed with yellow makes orange in the simple paint model.

stages.question: What color do yellow and blue paint make?
stages.feedback: Yellow mixed with blue makes green in the simple paint model.

clues.title: Colors across the wheel
clues.text: Complementary colors are across from each other on a color wheel. On a traditional artist's wheel, blue is across from orange, and red is across from green.

clues.title: Strong color pairs
clues.text: Opposite colors can stand out strongly beside each other. Try using one as the main color and the other for a small highlight.

stages.question: Which color is opposite blue on the traditional artist's wheel?
stages.feedback: Orange sits across from blue on the traditional artist's color wheel.

stages.question: Which color is opposite red on the traditional artist's wheel?
stages.feedback: Green is opposite red on the traditional artist's wheel.

stages.question: How can you use opposite colors without making a design too loud?
options: Use one most and the other as a small accent
Use both everywhere in equal amounts
Make every object a different color
stages.answer: Use one most and the other as a small accent
stages.feedback: One main color plus a smaller opposite-color accent is often easier to look at.

clues.title: Neighbors on the wheel
clues.text: Analogous colors sit next to each other on the color wheel. Blue, blue-green, and green are an example.

clues.title: A calm color group
clues.text: Neighboring colors often feel like they belong together. Pick one to be the main color and use the others to support it.

stages.question: Which set uses neighboring colors?
stages.feedback: Blue, blue-green, and green sit next to each other on the wheel.

stages.question: What does analogous mean in color theory?
options: Colors next to each other on the wheel
Colors that have no color in them
stages.answer: Colors next to each other on the wheel
stages.feedback: Analogous colors are neighbors on the color wheel.

stages.question: A design uses blue and green. Which color would fit as a nearby helper?
stages.feedback: Blue-green sits between blue and green, so it fits the neighboring-color group.

clues.title: Warm colors
clues.text: Red, orange, and yellow are often called warm colors. They can remind people of fire, sunlight, or a warm sunset.

clues.title: Cool colors
clues.text: Blue, blue-green, and many purples are often called cool colors. They can remind people of water, shade, or ice. These are feelings, not real temperatures.

stages.question: Which group is usually called warm?
stages.feedback: Red, orange, and yellow are commonly described as warm colors.

stages.question: Which color would help an icy scene feel cooler?
stages.feedback: Blue is often used to suggest coolness.

stages.question: Are warm and cool colors about the actual temperature of paint?
options: No, they describe the feeling a color can give
Yes, warm paint is physically hot
stages.answer: No, they describe the feeling a color can give
stages.feedback: Warm and cool are names for how colors can feel to us.

clues.title: Name, strength, and light
clues.text: Hue is the color family, like red or blue. Saturation tells how vivid or grayish a color looks. Value tells how light or dark it is.

clues.title: Change one thing
clues.text: A blue can stay blue but become softer by lowering saturation. It can also stay blue but become lighter by raising its value.

stages.question: Which word means the color family, like red or blue?
stages.feedback: Hue names the color family.

stages.question: A blue looks less vivid and more gray. What changed?
options: Its hue must have become yellow
stages.feedback: Lower saturation makes a color look less vivid.

stages.question: Which property tells how light or dark a color is?
stages.feedback: Value describes lightness and darkness.

clues.title: Value means light or dark
clues.text: Value tells how light or dark a color looks. Pale yellow has a high, light value. Deep navy has a low, dark value.

clues.title: Make things easy to see
clues.text: Strong value contrast means a light area sits beside a dark area. It can help words, shapes, and objects stand out.

stages.question: What does value describe?
options: How light or dark a color looks
How many colors are in a box
stages.answer: How light or dark a color looks
stages.feedback: Value is the lightness or darkness of a color.

stages.question: Which pair has the strongest light-dark contrast?
stages.feedback: White and black are far apart in value.

stages.question: Dark words on a pale sign are useful because they have…
stages.feedback: A big light-dark difference makes words easier to see.

clues.title: Make a tint
clues.text: A tint is made by adding white to a color. Red plus white makes a lighter pink tint.

clues.title: Make a shade
clues.text: A shade is made by adding black to a color. Blue plus black makes a darker blue shade.

stages.question: What can you add to red to make a pink tint?
stages.feedback: Adding white makes a tint lighter.

stages.question: What can you add to blue to make a darker shade?
stages.feedback: Adding black makes a shade darker.

stages.question: Which one is a tint of green?
stages.feedback: A tint is a color made lighter with white.

clues.title: Screens use light
clues.text: Phone, TV, and computer screens make colors with red, green, and blue light. This system is called RGB.

clues.title: Light adds together
clues.text: In the RGB light system, red light plus green light makes yellow. Red, green, and blue light together can make white on a screen.

stages.question: Which color system do screens use to mix light?
stages.feedback: Screens use red, green, and blue light: RGB.

stages.question: In RGB light, red light plus green light makes…
stages.feedback: Red and green light together look yellow in the RGB system.

stages.question: What can red, green, and blue light together make on a screen?
stages.feedback: Adding red, green, and blue light at full strength can make white.

clues.title: One color family
clues.text: A monochromatic palette uses one hue, such as blue, with different light and dark versions of that color.

clues.title: Keep it interesting
clues.text: A one-color design can still have variety. Try pale blue, medium blue, and deep blue so shapes do not all look the same.

stages.question: What is a monochromatic palette?
options: One hue shown in different lightness or darkness
Only colors opposite on the wheel
Every color in the rainbow at once
stages.answer: One hue shown in different lightness or darkness
stages.feedback: Monochromatic means using one hue with different values or strengths.

stages.question: Which group is monochromatic?
options: Pale blue, blue, and dark blue
stages.answer: Pale blue, blue, and dark blue
stages.feedback: All three examples use the blue hue in different versions.

stages.question: How can a one-color design show different objects?
options: Use lighter and darker versions of the hue
Make every part exactly the same
stages.answer: Use lighter and darker versions of the hue
stages.feedback: Different light and dark versions help objects stand apart.

clues.title: A palette is a plan
clues.text: A color palette is a group of colors chosen to work together in a picture, room, game, or poster.

clues.title: Choose with a reason
clues.text: A good palette fits what you want to show. A few chosen colors can feel clearer than many unrelated colors.

stages.question: What is a color palette?
options: A group of colors chosen to work together
stages.answer: A group of colors chosen to work together
stages.feedback: A palette is a planned group of colors.

stages.question: What is a good reason to choose colors?
options: They fit the mood or purpose
Use as many colors as possible
Pick colors with no plan every time
stages.answer: They fit the mood or purpose
stages.feedback: The job or feeling of a design can guide its palette.

stages.question: A poster feels messy because every object has a different bright color. What may help?
options: Use a smaller, planned group of colors
Make every word a different font color
stages.answer: Use a smaller, planned group of colors
stages.feedback: A smaller planned palette can make a design feel clearer.

clues.title: Mix two primary paints
clues.text: In the simple red-yellow-blue paint model, mixing two primary colors makes a secondary color.

clues.title: Remember the three mixes
clues.text: Red + yellow makes orange. Yellow + blue makes green. Blue + red makes purple.

stages.question: Which color is made by mixing red and yellow paint?
stages.feedback: Red and yellow make orange in the simple paint model.

stages.question: Which color is made by mixing blue and yellow paint?
stages.feedback: Blue and yellow make green.

stages.question: Which color is made by mixing blue and red paint?
stages.feedback: Blue and red make purple in the simple paint model.

clues.title: Help one thing stand out
clues.text: A focal point is the part of a picture you notice first. A brighter or more different color can help guide your eyes to it.

clues.title: Do not make everything shout
clues.text: If every object is equally bright and colorful, it is harder to know where to look. Let a few things be quieter so the main thing can stand out.

stages.question: What is a focal point?
options: The darkest edge of every picture
stages.feedback: The focal point is where the viewer's eyes are drawn first.

stages.question: How can you make a main object stand out?
options: Give it a clear color difference from its background
Make every object exactly as bright
Hide it behind the busiest pattern
stages.answer: Give it a clear color difference from its background
stages.feedback: A clear difference can help the main object be noticed.

stages.question: If everything is very bright and colorful, what may happen?
options: It may be hard to know where to look
stages.answer: It may be hard to know where to look
stages.feedback: Too many strong elements can compete for attention.

clues.title: Vivid and muted
clues.text: A color with high saturation looks strong and vivid. A color with low saturation looks softer, duller, or more gray.

clues.title: Choose the strength
clues.text: Use vivid colors when you want attention. Muted colors can work well in the background so the main object stands out.

stages.question: Which color has high saturation?
stages.feedback: High saturation means the color looks vivid.

stages.question: What happens when you lower a color's saturation?
options: It turns into its opposite color
stages.feedback: Lower saturation reduces how vivid a color looks.

stages.question: Where can muted colors be useful?
options: In the background behind a main object
stages.answer: In the background behind a main object
stages.feedback: Muted backgrounds can help the main subject stand out.

clues.title: Neutral colors
clues.text: Black, white, gray, and many browns are called neutral colors. They often do not feel as bright or colorful as strong reds or blues.

clues.title: Give colors room
clues.text: Neutral colors can help bright colors stand out. A gray wall, for example, lets a colorful picture become the focus.

stages.question: Which is a neutral color?
stages.feedback: Gray is a common neutral color.

stages.question: Which set is mostly neutral?
stages.feedback: Black, white, and gray are neutral colors.

stages.question: Why might a designer use a gray background?
options: To help bright objects stand out
Because gray is always the brightest color
stages.answer: To help bright objects stand out
stages.feedback: Neutral backgrounds can make colorful objects easier to notice.

clues.title: Colors can suggest a mood
clues.text: Many people connect blue with calm or cool feelings and orange with warmth or energy. These are common ideas, not rules for everyone.

clues.title: The surroundings matter
clues.text: A color can feel different next to another color or under different light. Think about the whole scene, not one color by itself.

stages.question: Which color is often used to suggest a calm, cool feeling?
stages.feedback: Blue is often used to suggest calm or cool feelings.

stages.question: Which color is often used to suggest warmth or energy?
stages.feedback: Orange is often linked with warmth or energy.

stages.question: Can the colors around a color change how it feels?
options: Yes, the surrounding colors and light matter
Only black can change a color
stages.answer: Yes, the surrounding colors and light matter
stages.feedback: The colors and light around something can affect how we see it.

clues.title: The color wheel
clues.text: A color wheel puts color families in a circle. It helps you see which colors are neighbors and which colors are opposite.

clues.title: Two useful relationships
clues.text: Neighbor colors can feel harmonious. Opposite colors can make a strong contrast. Both can be useful for different reasons.

stages.question: What can a color wheel help you see?
options: Which colors are neighbors or opposites
How heavy a paint tube is
stages.answer: Which colors are neighbors or opposites
stages.feedback: A color wheel shows color relationships.

stages.question: What do neighboring colors often create?
stages.feedback: Neighboring colors often feel like they belong together.

stages.question: What do opposite colors often create?
stages.feedback: Opposite colors usually stand out strongly beside each other.

clues.title: Mix red and yellow
clues.text: Red paint mixed with yellow paint makes orange in the simple artist's color model.

stages.question: What color do red and yellow paint make?
stages.feedback: Red and yellow make orange.

stages.question: Which paint would you add if an orange mix looks too yellow?
stages.feedback: A little red moves the mix toward orange.

stages.question: Is paint mixing the same as mixing screen light?
options: No, they use different color systems
Yes, they are exactly the same
stages.answer: No, they use different color systems
stages.feedback: Paint and screen light follow different mixing rules.

clues.title: Find the opposite
clues.text: Complementary colors sit across from each other on a color wheel. On the traditional artist's wheel, yellow and purple are opposites.

stages.question: Which color is opposite yellow on the traditional artist's wheel?
stages.feedback: Purple is opposite yellow on the traditional artist's wheel.

stages.question: What is special about complementary colors?
options: They sit across from each other on the wheel
stages.answer: They sit across from each other on the wheel
stages.feedback: Complementary colors are opposite colors on the wheel.

stages.question: What can complementary colors make when placed together?
stages.feedback: Opposite hues often create strong contrast.

clues.title: Use color neighbors
clues.text: Colors next to each other on the color wheel are called analogous. Red, red-orange, and orange are neighbors.

stages.question: Which set uses neighboring hues?
stages.feedback: Red, red-orange, and orange sit near one another on the wheel.

stages.question: What word means colors next to each other on the wheel?
stages.feedback: Analogous colors are neighbors on the wheel.

stages.question: What feeling can neighboring colors often give?
stages.feedback: Neighboring hues often make a cohesive palette.

clues.title: Cool colors
clues.text: Blue, blue-green, and cyan are often called cool colors. They can remind us of water, shade, or ice.

stages.question: Which color is often called cool?
stages.feedback: Blue is often described as cool.

stages.question: Which scene would blue help support?
stages.feedback: Blue often helps an icy scene feel cool.

stages.question: Does cool mean the paint is physically cold?
options: No, it describes the feeling of the color
Yes, the color changes room temperature
stages.answer: No, it describes the feeling of the color
stages.feedback: Cool color is a visual feeling, not the paint's actual temperature.

clues.title: Three ways to describe color
clues.text: Hue is the color family. Saturation is how vivid it looks. Value is how light or dark it looks.

stages.question: Which property means how vivid a color looks?
stages.feedback: Saturation describes vividness.

stages.question: Which property means light or dark?
stages.feedback: Value describes lightness and darkness.

stages.question: Which property means the color family, such as green?
stages.feedback: Hue names the color family.

clues.title: Light beside dark
clues.text: A light color beside a dark color creates value contrast. Strong value contrast can make signs and shapes easier to see.

stages.question: Which pair has strong value contrast?
stages.feedback: White and black have a big light-dark difference.

stages.question: What does value mean?
options: How light or dark a color looks
How many paint brushes you own
stages.answer: How light or dark a color looks
stages.feedback: Value is lightness or darkness.

stages.question: Why use contrast on a sign?
options: To make the sign easier to read
stages.answer: To make the sign easier to read
stages.feedback: Strong light-dark contrast helps text stand out.

clues.title: Add white for a tint
clues.text: A tint is a color mixed with white, making it lighter. Red plus white can make pink.

stages.question: What do you add to make a tint?
stages.feedback: A tint is made by adding white.

stages.question: Which is a tint of red?
stages.feedback: Pink is a lighter tint of red.

stages.question: Does a tint become lighter or darker?
stages.feedback: Adding white makes a color lighter.

clues.title: Add black for a shade
clues.text: A shade is made by mixing black into a color. It makes that color darker.

stages.question: What do you add to make a shade?
stages.feedback: A shade is made by adding black.

stages.question: What happens to a color when you add black?
stages.feedback: Black makes the color darker.

stages.question: Which is a shade of blue?
options: Pale sky blue made with white
stages.feedback: Dark navy is a darker version of blue.

clues.title: Red, green, and blue light
clues.text: Screens use red, green, and blue light to create colors. This is called RGB.

stages.question: What does RGB stand for?
stages.feedback: RGB stands for red, green, and blue.

stages.question: Which uses RGB light?
stages.feedback: Phone and computer screens use RGB light.

stages.question: Red and green light together make what color on a screen?
stages.feedback: Red and green light combine to look yellow.

clues.title: One hue, many versions
clues.text: A monochromatic palette uses one hue, like blue, with lighter and darker versions of that same hue.

stages.question: What does monochromatic mean?
options: Using one hue in different versions
stages.answer: Using one hue in different versions
stages.feedback: Monochromatic means one hue with variations.

stages.question: Which palette is monochromatic?
stages.feedback: The first set uses different versions of blue.

stages.question: How can you make a one-color picture interesting?
stages.feedback: Light and dark versions make the picture easier to read.

clues.title: Help the main thing stand out
clues.text: A focal point is the part you notice first. A different or brighter color can help draw your eyes to it.

stages.question: What is a focal point?
stages.feedback: A focal point is where your eyes go first.

stages.question: How can a game show which item matters most?
options: Make that item stand out from its surroundings
stages.answer: Make that item stand out from its surroundings
stages.feedback: A clear difference helps guide attention.

stages.question: What can happen if everything is equally loud in color?
options: It is harder to know where to look
The main object is always clear
stages.answer: It is harder to know where to look
stages.feedback: When everything competes, the main subject can be hard to spot.

clues.title: Make green with paint
clues.text: In the simple artist's paint model, yellow paint mixed with blue paint makes green.

stages.question: Which two paint colors make green?
stages.feedback: Yellow and blue make green in the simple paint model.

stages.question: Is green a primary or secondary color in the simple RYB paint model?
stages.feedback: Green is made by mixing two primary paints, so it is secondary.

stages.question: Which pair makes orange?
stages.feedback: Red and yellow make orange.

clues.title: Make a color softer
clues.text: Lower saturation makes a color less vivid and more muted. High saturation makes it look strong and bright in color.

stages.question: What does low saturation look like?
stages.feedback: Low saturation makes a color look less vivid.

stages.question: What does high saturation look like?
stages.feedback: High saturation means the color looks vivid.

stages.question: Where can a less saturated color work well?
stages.feedback: Muted colors can keep a background from competing with the main object.

clues.title: Neutral colors
clues.text: Gray, black, and white are common neutral colors. They often work well behind stronger, brighter colors.

stages.question: Which is a neutral color?
stages.feedback: Gray is a neutral color.

stages.question: Which group is neutral?
stages.feedback: Black, white, and gray are neutral colors.

stages.question: What can a gray background help do?
options: Let a bright picture stand out
Make every color brighter by itself
stages.answer: Let a bright picture stand out
stages.feedback: Neutral backgrounds can help colorful things stand out.

clues.title: Colors can suggest feelings
clues.text: Blue can suggest calm or cool feelings. Orange can suggest warmth or energy. People can feel differently, so these are common ideas rather than strict rules.

stages.question: Which color is often used to suggest calm?
stages.feedback: Blue is often used for calm scenes.

stages.question: Which color is often used to suggest warmth?
stages.feedback: Orange is often linked to warmth.

stages.question: Are color feelings exactly the same for everyone?
options: No, people and cultures can see colors differently
Yes, everyone always feels the same
Only children can feel color mood
stages.answer: No, people and cultures can see colors differently
stages.feedback: Color mood can depend on the person, culture, and context.

clues.title: Neighboring sunset colors
clues.text: Yellow, yellow-orange, and orange sit next to each other on the color wheel. These neighboring hues can make a smooth sunset palette.

stages.question: Which set fits a neighboring-color sunset palette?
stages.feedback: Yellow, yellow-orange, and orange are neighbors on the wheel.

stages.question: What are neighboring colors called?
stages.feedback: Analogous colors sit next to each other on the wheel.

stages.question: Why might these colors work for a sunset?
options: They are all opposite each other
stages.feedback: Neighboring warm hues can make a sunset feel connected.
